channel.title: Heather Lyn Wilson
channel.description: Faith, leadership, and what stood out from my Bible reading. New posts Monday, Wednesday, and Friday.

item.title: Isaiah 8:11-12
item.description: We are consuming so much of the same content, watching the same shows, scrolling the same feeds, following the same voices, that our thinking has quietly conformed to the world around us without us even noticing.

item.title: Isaiah 8:7
item.description: God's care can look small and quiet compared to what the world offers. But the world's power always comes with a price. What we think will save us often ends up overwhelming us.

item.title: Isaiah 7:3
item.description: I did not know Isaiah had a son. That was the first thing that caught me. I have read Isaiah more than a few times, but I never really stopped to think about the fact that he was a dad.

item.title: Ecclesiastes 7:18
item.description: Trying to be too good, in the sense of trying to earn God's love, is its own kind of trap. It looks holy on the outside. But underneath, it is prideful. It is exhausting. It is performative.

item.title: Proverbs 30:4
item.description: We tend to think of Jesus as a New Testament reveal. But this verse says otherwise. The Son was always there. The Old Testament was slowly asking a question. Jesus was always the answer.

item.title: Proverbs 20:3
item.description: It takes strength to walk away. It takes real self control to not engage. Anyone can pop off. Anyone can throw punches back. That is not honor. That is just reaction.

item.title: Proverbs 18:13
item.description: We post before we research. We repost before we read the article. We form strong opinions in about four seconds and then broadcast them to everyone we know. And Proverbs calls it what it is. Foolish.

item.title: Proverbs 11:24
item.description: The most generous people I know are also the most joyful, the most peaceful, the most alive. They give freely. And they always seem to have more, not less. Generosity multiplies. Stinginess shrinks.

item.title: Proverbs 1:31
item.description: The very lifestyle that promised to set everyone free is producing a generation that cannot get out of bed without medication. That is not a coincidence. It is the exact fruit Proverbs described thousands of years ago.

item.title: Psalm 141:5
item.description: We say we want to grow, and be sharpened. We would tell you we want to be more like Jesus. But when someone actually walks up and tells us something hard about ourselves, most of us get defensive. David does the opposite.

item.title: Psalm 138:8
item.description: The reason God is going to work out His plans for my life is not tied to how well I am performing. It is tied to who He is. His faithful love endures forever. His involvement in my life is not conditional on me.

item.title: Psalm 119:140
item.description: The promises that carried Abraham are the same ones that carry me. The promises that steadied David are the same ones that steady me. The promises that gave Paul confidence in a prison cell are the same ones that give me confidence in my own life today.

item.title: Psalm 73:28
item.description: Being close to God and being covered by God changes what comes out of our mouths. If we are truly close to Him, and truly sheltered by Him, we cannot help but talk about Him. It leaks out.

item.title: Psalm 71:18
item.description: Everything you have walked through, every prayer God answered, every hard thing He carried you through — it was not just for you. It was so you would have something to hand to the ones coming next.

item.title: Psalm 59:12
item.description: Pride does not free people. It captures them. That is a very different picture than the one our culture is painting.

item.title: Psalm 56:4
item.description: They can hurt me. They can lie about me. They can walk away. They can make my life difficult in a thousand ways. But they cannot touch the part of me that belongs to God.

item.title: Psalm 50:14 & 23
item.description: Everything in you wants to focus on what is going wrong. And in that moment, choosing thankfulness costs something. You are laying down your right to complain. That kind of thankfulness is worship.

item.title: Psalm 40:5
item.description: He answers a prayer and we say thank you and get on with our day. He rescues us and we exhale and go back to normal. We forget. Not because we are ungrateful. Just because we are moving.

item.title: Psalm 33:10
item.description: Panic assumes God is not in charge. Faith assumes He is. And when I remember that He frustrates the plans of the nations, I can breathe again.

item.title: Not Clapbacks or Receipts
item.description: Because a life of integrity doesn't need to defend itself the way a life without it does. The truth stands on its own over time, and character speaks louder than accusations.
